chief_complaint: involuntary leakage of urine when coughing, laughing, sneezing, or lifting heavy boxes
hpi_details: She has leakage only with coughing, laughing, sneezing, and lifting. She has had three vaginal deliveries and has no dysuria, fever, hematuria, pelvic pain, urgency, or urge leakage. She is considering an outpatient mid-urethral sling after conservative treatment has not provided enough relief.
ideas: thinks this is stress urinary incontinence and wants to know whether a sling is appropriate
concerns: She is anxious that having surgical mesh or tape implanted might cause permanent nerve pain or foreign-body complications.
expectations: wants to understand conservative and surgical options, recovery, and complications

clinical_knowledge.topic: Stress urinary incontinence: evaluation and shared decision-making about a mid-urethral sling
core_concepts: Stress incontinence is leakage with increased abdominal pressure; urgency-predominant leakage suggests urge or mixed incontinence instead.

Initial assessment includes history, urinalysis when infection or hematuria is possible, pelvic examination with cough stress test, assessment for prolapse, and post-void residual when voiding dysfunction is suspected.
First-line treatment includes pelvic-floor muscle training, weight and constipation management when relevant, and continence products; surgery is elective and should follow shared decision-making.
A synthetic mid-urethral sling can be effective for appropriately selected women, but counseling must cover mesh exposure/erosion, pain, urinary retention, de novo urgency, failure, and alternatives.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: involuntary leakage of urine when coughing, laughing, sneezing, or lifting heavy boxes
Leakage occurs with cough, laugh, sneeze, and lifting, without urgency or infectious symptoms.
Three vaginal deliveries are a recognized risk factor; pelvic examination should assess prolapse and demonstrate stress leakage when possible.
common_misconceptions: Calling all leakage a urinary tract infection or prescribing antibiotics without symptoms and testing consistent with infection.
Assuming urodynamics are required before every uncomplicated primary stress-incontinence surgery.
Presenting sling surgery as mandatory or risk-free rather than one elective option.
dangerous_errors: Missing gross hematuria, recurrent infections, pelvic mass, neurologic symptoms, significant prolapse, or elevated residual that warrants further evaluation.
Proceeding with surgery during an active urinary infection or without discussing the possibility of postoperative voiding dysfunction.
Treating acute inability to void, fever with systemic illness, or severe pelvic pain as routine incontinence.
management_principles: Confirm the predominant symptom pattern, perform urinalysis when indicated, and assess pelvic support and emptying before selecting treatment.
Offer supervised pelvic-floor muscle training and modifiable-risk counseling before or alongside referral for surgical options.
If she chooses a sling, arrange urogynecology/urology counseling, review prior pelvic surgery and future pregnancy plans, and give clear postoperative retention and infection return precautions.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Pregnancy and plans for future pregnancy should be discussed because they may influence timing and choice of surgery.

Hematuria, recurrent UTI, prior pelvic radiation, neurologic disease, prior incontinence surgery, significant prolapse, or voiding symptoms make this a complicated presentation and may require specialist testing.

source_refs.title: American Urological Association: Stress Urinary Incontinence Guideline

reference_soap.subjective: 48-year-old G3P3 with leakage only on cough, laugh, sneeze, and lifting. She denies urgency, dysuria, fever, hematuria, and pelvic pain; conservative measures have not adequately relieved symptoms.
reference_soap.objective: Obtain vitals and urinalysis if clinically indicated. Perform pelvic examination with cough stress test, assess for prolapse, and measure post-void residual if voiding symptoms are present.
reference_soap.assessment: Uncomplicated stress urinary incontinence; no features supplied to suggest infection, urgency-predominant incontinence, or an acute urologic emergency.
reference_soap.plan: Discuss pelvic-floor muscle training and lifestyle measures. Refer for elective sling counseling if she desires surgery after informed discussion of alternatives and mesh/voiding risks; seek urgent care for inability to void, systemic infection symptoms, severe pain, or gross hematuria.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical features of stress urinary incontinence and distinguish it from urge and mixed incontinence
Formulate prioritized differential diagnosis for involuntary leakage of urine when coughing, laughing, sneezing, or lifting heavy boxes
Select focused evaluation, including when urinalysis, pelvic examination, or post-void residual is appropriate
Use shared decision-making for conservative treatment and elective sling referral

teaching.one_liner: A 48-year-old woman with three prior vaginal deliveries has predictable leakage with exertion and no urgency or infectious symptoms, consistent with stress urinary incontinence.

must_ask.say: Does the leaking happen specifically when you cough, laugh, sneeze, or lift something heavy?
Do you also get sudden, strong urges to urinate that you can't hold, separate from the leaking with activity?
How many vaginal deliveries have you had, and have you had any pelvic or bladder surgery before?
How many pads do you need to use each day because of the leakage?

must_ask.objective: Impact on activity and treatment expectations
must_ask.say: How is this affecting your exercise or daily activities, and what are you hoping treatment can achieve?

No, my urine stream is strong and steady, and I never have to push or wait for it to start.
No, my bladder feels completely empty after I go, and it doesn't dribble afterward.
No, I can always urinate without any trouble, and my lower belly never hurts or feels bloated.
I urinate about four or five times during the day and rarely wake up at night to go.
No, I never get a sudden desperate urge to pee, and I never leak on my way to the bathroom.
It happens whenever I cough, sneeze, laugh hard, or lift heavy boxes.
It is usually a small squirt each time, but I wear one or two panty liners every day to stay dry.
No, I have no burning pain when I pee, no blood in my urine, and no fever.
No back pain, no leg weakness or numbness, and my bowel control is completely normal.
No, my bowels move regularly every day, and I don't suffer from constipation.
I drink about five glasses of water and one cup of morning coffee, and I avoid drinking fluids right before bedtime.
No, I have not taken any cold pills, decongestants, allergy medicines, antidepressants, or water pills.

No, I have never had any surgeries on my bladder, uterus, or pelvis.
No, I have never felt a bulge, fullness, or the feeling of something falling out of my vagina.

I think this is stress incontinence, and I am wondering if a mid-urethral sling surgery would be right for me.

I have high blood pressure and mild high cholesterol, both managed well.

No, I have never smoked.

Both of my parents had high blood pressure, but no one in my family had bladder or kidney issues.
My menstrual periods are regular every twenty-eight days, and my last period began two weeks ago.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 128/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 99% on room air, and temperature 36.6 degrees Celsius.
Abdomen is soft, flat, and non-tender, with no palpable bladder distension or suprapubic mass.
Tympanic percussion note throughout the abdomen with no suprapubic dullness to suggest urinary retention.
No costovertebral angle tenderness on either side.
Normal external genitalia and well-estrogenized vaginal mucosa without pelvic organ prolapse, but immediate spurts of urine leak from the urethral meatus during cough stress testing.
Motor strength is 5/5 in all bilateral lower extremity muscle groups.
Intact light touch and pinprick sensation throughout both lower extremities and the perineal saddle region.
Patellar and Achilles deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally, with downward-going plantar responses.
Normal resting and squeeze anal sphincter tone, with intact anal wink reflex and no stool impaction.
